signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The G10 scorecard reveals an acute divergence with USD up +2.017% across 9 pairs while NOK averages -2.038% across 2 pairs, generating a 4.055% leader-to-laggard spread. Strait of Hormuz naval mine detonations and tanker fires elevate geopolitical supply risks, yet broad dollar demand decisively outweighs crude resilience. On a policy level, Fed policy rate at 4.00% vs Norges Bank 4.5% yields a -50bp nominal carry deficit for the dollar, but US 5Y yields rose +26bp over 5D (FRED, as of Nov 12) split into real +25bp and breakeven +1bp, demonstrating strong real-yield-led momentum. USD/NOK trades at 9.565, closing above its SMA20 (9.368), SMA50 (9.422), and SMA200 (9.486) in an extended technical posture. Retail sentiment shows an extreme 91% long bias on USD/NOK, highlighting late-stage chasing conditions. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK; broad USD strength and real-rate momentum dominate despite extended technicals. Catalyst: US Retail Sales release tomorrow. Risk: Rapid de-escalation in Middle East shipping corridors alongside a sharp rebound in European risk assets compresses the 4.055% G10 spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.62, holding above its SMA20 (158.22), SMA50 (157.42), and SMA200 (158.72) moving average cluster. SOFR at 3.90% vs TONA at 1.23% delivers a +267bp carry advantage that firmly favors the USD, keeping the underlying trend supported while VIX remains contained at 19.3 (normal volatility). Saxo 25d risk reversals show a pronounced -1.79 put skew, signaling heavy institutional demand for downside protection even as spot tests intervention-sensitive territory. Speculative positioning via CFTC shows JPY Leveraged Funds net short -21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile (z +1.46) of its 52-week range, reflecting crowded short exposure. Watch 160.00 as the critical barrier that previously triggered verbal intervention warnings from Japanese authorities. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; wide OIS carry premium sustains the upward grind while VIX holds below 25. Catalyst: Japan Q3 GDP release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot closes above 160.00 and sparks direct Ministry of Finance currency intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1031, positioned entirely below its SMA20 (1.1174), SMA50 (1.1297), and SMA200 (1.1527) in a clear technical downtrend. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short -104,030 contracts (week ending Nov 03), standing at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z -1.80) after a 4W reduction of -19,255 contracts, confirming an extremely crowded institutional short. In stark contrast, retail positioning sits at an extreme 87% long, setting up an acute institutional versus retail positioning divergence. Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a +135bp nominal carry spread in favor of the dollar (SOFR vs €STR spread at +146bp), structurally limiting upside momentum. Options pricing reflects moderate hedging demand with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.2% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.3%, generating a +0.9% vol risk premium. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent carry headwind and institutional short trend outweigh contrarian retail positioning. Catalyst: Euro Area Industrial Production and ZEW Economic Sentiment releases tomorrow. Risk: A close back above the 20-day SMA at 1.1174 triggers an aggressive short-covering squeeze among leveraged funds.

signals.title: GBP/USD — BoE Hawk Repricing + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3223, breaking below its key moving average cluster of SMA20 (1.3361), SMA50 (1.3341), and SMA200 (1.3413) to confirm an established technical downtrend. Bank of England Chief Economist Pill stated the BoE should have raised borrowing costs earlier, reinforcing hawkish policy expectations with BoE at 4.00% (HIKING) vs Fed at 4.00% (ON HOLD). Front-end rates mirror this shift, with the UK-US 2Y yield spread widening +12bp over the last 5 sessions to +25bp. CFTC Leveraged Funds remain net long +32,686 contracts (week ending Nov 03), having added +12,670 contracts WoW, creating an unwinding hazard as price continues to slide. Options show a mild put skew with 25d risk reversals at -0.55, reflecting institutional caution against sterling spot weakness. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish GBP/USD; technical breakdown below the 200-day SMA counters hawkish BoE rhetoric. Catalyst: UK Labour Market Report (Average Weekly Earnings and Unemployment) at 07:00 UTC. Risk: Strong wage growth data accelerates BoE hike pricing and lifts spot back above 1.3340.
